title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Sales Contract Dispute Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: Where there is no written contract between the parties, and one party claims the existence of a sales contract relationship on the basis of delivery notes, receipt notes, settlement statements, invoices, etc., the People's Court shall, taking into account the transaction method, transaction practices between the parties, and other relevant evidence, determine whether the sales contract is concluded.
Where a confirmation letter of account reconciliation, a debt confirmation letter, or other such correspondence or voucher does not record the name of the creditor, and one party to the sales contract uses it to prove the existence of a sales contract relationship, the People's Court shall support such claim, unless there is sufficient contrary evidence to rebut it.
II. Delivery of Subject Matter and Transfer of Ownership

Article 2: Where the subject matter is an electronic information product that does not require delivery through a tangible carrier, the parties have not clearly agreed on the delivery method, and the matter still cannot be determined in accordance with Article 510 of the Civil Code, delivery shall be deemed to have been made upon the buyer's receipt of the agreed electronic information product or the right certificate.

Article 3: In accordance with Article 629 of the Civil Code, where the buyer refuses to accept the excess part of the subject matter, the buyer may keep the excess part of the subject matter in custody on behalf of the seller. Where the buyer claims that the seller shall bear the reasonable expenses incurred during the period of custodianship, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where the buyer claims that the seller shall bear losses caused during the period of custodianship not due to the buyer's intentional act or gross negligence, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 4: The "relevant documents and materials other than the documents for taking delivery of the subject matter" as provided in Article 599 of the Civil Code shall mainly include the insurance policy, warranty certificate, ordinary invoice, special VAT invoice, product certificate of conformity, quality guarantee letter, quality appraisal certificate, quality inspection certificate, product import and export quarantine certificate, certificate of origin, instruction manual, packing list, and the like.

Article 5: Where the seller proves that it has performed its obligation to deliver the subject matter solely on the basis of special VAT invoices and tax deduction materials, and the buyer does not accept this, the seller shall provide other evidence to prove the fact of delivery of the subject matter.
Where the contract stipulates, or the parties are accustomed to using an ordinary invoice as proof of payment, and the buyer uses an ordinary invoice to prove that it has performed its payment obligation, the People's Court shall support such claim, unless there is sufficient contrary evidence to rebut it.

Article 8: The phrase "where the subject matter needs to be transported" as provided in subparagraph (1) of paragraph 2 of Article 603 of the Civil Code refers to the circumstance where the seller is responsible for arranging consignment of the subject matter, and the carrier is a transport operator independent of the parties to the sales contract. The risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be handled in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 607 of the Civil Code.

Article 9: Where, in accordance with the contract, the seller transports the subject matter to the place designated by the buyer and delivers it to the carrier, the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter shall be borne by the buyer, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 10: Where the seller sells subject matter in transit that has been handed over to a carrier for transport, and at the time of formation of the contract, the seller knew or should have known that the subject matter had already been damaged or lost but failed to inform the buyer, and the buyer claims that the seller shall bear the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 11: Where the parties have not agreed on the risk bearing, the subject matter is fungible goods, and the seller has not clearly identified the subject matter to the sales contract in an identifiable manner such as through shipping documents, affixing marks, or notifying the buyer, and the buyer claims that it shall not bear the risk of damage to or loss of the subject matter, the People's Court shall support the claim.
IV. Inspection of the Subject Matter

Article 12: When the People's Court specifically determines the "reasonable period" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 621 of the Civil Code, it shall make a judgment in accordance with the principle of good faith by comprehensively considering the nature of the transaction between the parties, the purpose of the transaction, the transaction method, transaction practices, the kind, quantity, and nature of the subject matter, the installation and usage conditions, the nature of the defects, the duty of reasonable care owed by the buyer, the inspection method and its difficulty, the specific environment and skills of the buyer or the inspector, and other reasonable factors.
The "two years" provided in paragraph 2 of Article 621 of the Civil Code is the longest reasonable period. Such period is a fixed period and shall not be subject to the provisions on suspension, interruption, or extension of the limitation of action.

Article 13: Where the buyer raises an objection within a reasonable period, and the seller claims that the buyer has waived the objection on the grounds that the buyer has paid the price, confirmed the amount of debt, used the subject matter, etc., the People's Court shall not support the seller's claim, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 14: After the inspection period, reasonable period, or two-year period provided in Article 621 of the Civil Code has elapsed, where the buyer claims that the quantity or quality of the subject matter does not conform to the agreement, the People's Court shall not support the claim.
Where the seller voluntarily bears liability for breach of contract and later reneges on the ground that the aforementioned period has elapsed, the People's Court shall not support such reneging.
V. Liability for Breach of Contract

Article 15: Where the buyer retains part of the price as a quality guarantee deposit in accordance with the contract, and the seller fails to resolve the quality problem in a timely manner during the quality guarantee period, thereby affecting the value or use effect of the subject matter, and the seller claims payment of such part of the price, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 16: Where the buyer raises a quality objection within the inspection period, quality guarantee period, or reasonable period, and the seller fails to make repairs as required, or due to urgent circumstances, the buyer repairs the subject matter itself or through a third party, and then claims that the seller shall bear the reasonable expenses incurred as a result, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 17: Where the quality of the subject matter does not conform to the agreement, and the buyer requests a reduction in price in accordance with Article 582 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support the claim. Where a party claims that the price difference shall be calculated based on the market value at the time of delivery between the subject matter conforming to the agreement and the subject matter actually delivered, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where the price has already been paid, and the buyer claims restitution of the excess portion of the price after the price reduction, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 18: Any change made by the sales contract to the time limit for payment shall not affect the parties' agreement on liquidated damages for overdue payment, but the starting point for calculating such liquidated damages shall be changed accordingly.
Where the sales contract provides for liquidated damages for overdue payment, and the buyer refuses to pay such liquidated damages on the ground that the seller did not claim liquidated damages for overdue payment when accepting the price, the People's Court shall not support the refusal.
Where the sales contract provides for liquidated damages for overdue payment, but the statement of account, repayment agreement, or the like does not involve liability for overdue payment, and the seller, when claiming the debt based on the statement of account, repayment agreement, or the like, requests the buyer to pay liquidated damages for overdue payment in accordance with the contract, the People's Court shall support the claim, except where the statement of account, repayment agreement, or the like expressly records the amount of principal and interest for overdue payment or has changed the provisions of the sales contract concerning principal and interest.
Where the sales contract does not provide for liquidated damages for overdue payment or the method for calculating such liquidated damages, and the seller claims compensation for losses from overdue payment on the ground of the buyer's breach of contract, if the breaching act occurred before August 19, 2019, the People's Court may calculate the losses based on the benchmark interest rate for RMB loans of the same type and term of the People's Bank of China, with reference to the standard of overdue penalty interest rate; if the breaching act occurred after August 20, 2019, the People's Court may calculate the losses from overdue payment based on the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center under the authorization of the People's Bank of China at the time of the breaching act, plus 30-50%.

Article 19: Where the seller fails to perform or improperly performs its ancillary obligation, causing the buyer to be unable to realize the purpose of the contract, and the buyer claims dissolution of the contract, the People's Court shall support the claim in accordance with subparagraph (4) of paragraph 1 of Article 563 of the Civil Code.

Article 20: After the sales contract is dissolved due to breach of contract, where the non-breaching party claims that the liquidated damages clause shall continue to apply, the People's Court shall support the claim; however, if the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused, the People's Court may handle the matter in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 585 of the Civil Code.

Article 21: Where one party to a sales contract claims payment of liquidated damages on the ground of the other party's breach, and the other party makes a defense for exemption from liability on the grounds that the contract was not formed, the contract has not taken effect, the contract is void, or no breach of contract was committed, without claiming adjustment of excessively high liquidated damages, the People's Court shall provide clarification as to whether the party needs to claim adjustment of liquidated damages if the court does not uphold the defense for exemption from liability.
Where the court of first instance considers that the defense for exemption from liability is established and fails to provide clarification, and the court of second instance considers that judgment should be rendered for payment of liquidated damages, the court of second instance may directly provide clarification and amend the judgment.

Article 22: Where one party to a sales contract causes losses to the other party by breaching the contract, and the other party claims compensation for loss of expected benefits, the People's Court, when determining the scope of liability for breach of contract, shall make a determination in accordance with the party's claim and pursuant to Articles 584, 591, and 592 of the Civil Code and Article 23 of this Interpretation.

Article 23: Where one party to a sales contract gains benefits as a result of the other party's breach, and the breaching party claims that such benefits shall be deducted from the amount of damages, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 24: Where the buyer knew or should have known at the time of concluding the contract that the quality of the subject matter had defects, and claims that the seller shall bear warranty liability for defects, the People's Court shall not support the claim, unless the buyer did not know at the time of concluding the contract that such defects would cause a significant reduction in the basic utility of the subject matter.
VI. Retention of Ownership

Article 25: Where a party to a sales contract claims that the provisions of Article 641 of the Civil Code on retention of ownership of the subject matter apply to immovable property, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 26: Where the buyer has paid more than 75% of the total price of the subject matter, and the seller claims to take back the subject matter, the People's Court shall not support the claim.
Under the circumstances of subparagraph (3) of paragraph 1 of Article 642 of the Civil Code, where a third party has already acquired the ownership or other real right of the subject matter in good faith in accordance with Article 311 of the Civil Code, and the seller claims to take back the subject matter, the People's Court shall not support the claim.
VII. Special Sales

Article 27: The "payment by installments" as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 634 of the Civil Code refers to the buyer paying the total price payable to the seller in at least three installments within a certain period.
Where the provisions of a contract for sale by installments violate paragraph 1 of Article 634 of the Civil Code and harm the buyer's interests, and the buyer claims that such provisions are void, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 28: Where a contract for sale by installments stipulates that the seller may withhold the price already received when dissolving the contract, and the amount withheld by the seller exceeds the usage fee of the subject matter and the amount of compensation for damage to the subject matter, and the buyer requests restitution of the excess portion, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where the parties have not agreed on the usage fee of the subject matter, the People's Court may determine it by reference to the local rental standard for similar subject matter.

Article 29: Where the quality of the sample as agreed in the contract is inconsistent with the written description, and the parties cannot reach an agreement when a dispute arises, if the appearance and intrinsic quality of the sealed sample have not changed, the People's Court shall take the sample as the standard; if the appearance and intrinsic quality have changed, or the parties dispute whether a change has occurred and it cannot be ascertained, the People's Court shall take the written description as the standard.

Article 32: Where laws or administrative regulations have provisions on contracts for transfer of rights such as assignment of claims and transfer of equity, such provisions shall apply; where there are no such provisions, the People's Court may, in accordance with Articles 467 and 646 of the Civil Code, apply the relevant provisions on sales contracts by reference.
Where the relevant provisions on sales contracts are applied by reference to a transfer of rights or other onerous contract, the People's Court shall first cite Article 646 of the Civil Code, and then cite the relevant provisions on sales contracts.

Article 33: Where the provisions issued by this Court before this Interpretation came into force concerning contracts such as purchase and sales contracts and sales contracts that transfer ownership of the subject matter for value conflict with this Interpretation, such provisions shall no longer apply from the date on which this Interpretation comes into force.
For cases of sales contract disputes that have not been finally adjudicated after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall apply; for cases that have been finally adjudicated before this Interpretation comes into force, and for which a party applies for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, this Interpretation shall not apply.
